title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Condition Report. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Condition Report
options.thesis: The answer is a report of what was examined. What was not examined stays blank.
options.viewport: Ask is one sheet. The question is the object. Each row is a passage and its location. A blank row means not examined.
options.risk: Turns into a museum label and the question stops being something you ask.

raised.raise: A remark with no citation stays visibly unexamined. It never balances into an answer.
Opening a citation reveals the passage on the sheet, in place.
Earlier runs stay on the sheet as lighter marks. The live question is the heavy mark.
One ink. State is the weight of a mark, not a colored chip.

options.label: The Exhibit Binder
options.thesis: The answer is an exhibit. The number in the margin is the citation.
options.viewport: Ask is an open binder. The question sits at the top. The returned passage is an exhibit with its tab and page number.
options.risk: Also the legal-folder template most evidence products reach for.

options.label: The Coupon Wallet
options.thesis: The question is a coupon. A refusal is a VOID stamp. Nothing is deleted.
options.viewport: Ask is one coupon in a wallet. Validated fields hold the citation. A refusal stamps VOID across the coupon and leaves it in the book.
options.case: VOID is a clearer refusal than a blank row. Weaker identification: another travel paper after the strip bay.
options.risk: Becomes a souvenir ticket and the passage has nowhere to be read.

options.label: The Select Rail
options.thesis: Passages are frames on a rail. A grease cross is cited. A punched corner is not allowed.
options.viewport: Ask is a rail of frames. The flag marks where you stopped. Set-aside passages hang on pins below. Copy sits only in the white windows.
options.case: Clearer run states than a report sheet. Weaker identification: a film bench is not this desk.
options.risk: The orange field becomes a theme and the passage is too small to read.

options.label: The Tension Column
options.lineage: a tensegrity column of rods and cord
options.viewport: Claims float apart until a citation pulls them taut.
options.case: Members do not recognize a sculpture, and a force diagram hides the passage.
options.kept: A claim with no counterforce stays slack.
options.risk: The answer becomes a diagram of tension and the document never opens.

options.label: The Cloud Quarry
options.viewport: A saw opens a block and either a passage or an empty sky falls out.
options.case: Weather is not this desk, and a dissolving building cannot hold a citation.
options.kept: Inspection reveals the interior in place.
options.risk: The product becomes a dream and access has no field.

options.label: The Scrawled Sleeve
options.lineage: a flash photo defaced with marker
options.viewport: The answer is a photograph written over in marker.
options.case: A nightclub sleeve is not a company desk, and scrawl hides the evidence.
options.kept: History stays on the surface. The live mark is heavier.

options.label: The Glyph Grid
options.lineage: a scene drawn in typewriter characters
options.viewport: The answer is a picture made of characters.
options.case: Members do not read phosphor portraits, and the citation stops being a sentence.
options.kept: One grid and one ink. Emphasis is density, not a second palette.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A chat thread, a left rail, source chips, and a citation drawer, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: Ask is a message list. You type at the bottom. Citations open in a side drawer.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other assistant, by design.
